forecast.reasoning: Start from scout's own admitted gap: no tracker-sourced est_monthly_units exists for this term, so term_monthly_units (14,400-33,600, base 24,000) is genius's own order-of-magnitude read of the standing page-one competitive set, widened ±40% per the kb's mandated method. From there, attainable share is placed using the buyer's own CTR/ATC/buy judgement: click=0.35 is moderate (the stamped-steel buckle thumbnail is a real pattern-break per three_second_scan, but zero reviews and a 1.7-2.2x price anchor pull back some clicks), while add_to_cart=0.4 and buy=0.5 are above-median once the listing's bullets answer the buyer's top fears — so share starts in the lower-middle of the kb's 1-5% band by month 6 (2-6%) and climbs into the kb's 3-10% band by month 12 (4-10%) as reviews accumulate and cross moore.chasm. Multiplying term volume by share gives month-6 units of 288-2,016 (base 840) and month-12 units of 576-3,360 (base 1,680). Integrating a ramp curve across the year (innovator-only months 1-3, ramping through months 4-6 to the month-6 rate, then ramping months 7-12 toward the month-12 rate) gives annual_units_y1 of roughly 3,500-22,800 units (base ~10,300) — a wide range that should be treated as the honest uncertainty of a brand-new, zero-review entrant rather than narrowed prematurely.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and a copycat factory reverse-engineered the visible radiused-anchor, face-stamped buckle within 90 days and is selling a near-identical steel-buckle strap at 60% of our price; buyers can no longer tell the two apart in the search-results thumbnail.
premortem.mitigation: Extend the FTO search into a provisional design-patent filing on the radiused-anchor + emboss-legend combination, own the production die so a copier needs its own tooling lead time too, and move on review velocity fast enough that social proof (not just the visual) becomes the moat before a copy can catch up.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Provisional design-patent filing fee, adjunct to the FTO search already budgeted in tooling_and_nre.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the printed belly-band plus box contents pushed the outer carton a few millimetres over the small-standard size-tier line, and the FBA fee jump on every single unit erased the margin nobody modeled.
premortem.mitigation: Lock final packaging dimensions against the FBA size-tier cutoff with a 3-5mm safety margin before ordering belly-bands/cartons, and get a physical FBA dimensioner check on a pre-production sample before the first inbound shipment.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the Section 301 rate on our HTS line moved from 7.5% toward the higher end of the published 7.5%-100% band (F14), and the extra duty line alone erased the contribution margin the plan launched on.
premortem.mitigation: Landed_cost_usd.high already prices the wide duty/tariff band; keep price flexible to absorb a step-up, and hold a qualified Vietnam-based backup supplier quote in reserve as a 6-12 month contingency so origin can shift without a full re-sourcing cycle.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and Amazon flagged the '150KG PER BUCKLE, pull-tested' claim as an unsubstantiated safety/performance claim and suppressed the listing pending documentation, freezing sales for three weeks during peak season.
premortem.mitigation: Commission the third-party 1,000-cycle pull-test/fatigue report (already in tooling_and_nre) before the listing goes live, keep the certificate on file for a fast appeal, and phrase the claim exactly as tested ('pull-tested to 150kg per buckle') rather than as a weight-capacity or safety guarantee.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Cost is already fully captured in the destructive-test lab-fee line in tooling_and_nre; zero incremental spend.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and review count never crossed roughly 30 (moore.chasm), so the listing stayed stuck on page two next to competitors with hundreds of reviews, and the paid-traffic cost of trying to hold page-one visibility ate every dollar of contribution.
premortem.mitigation: Deliberately run the first-60-90-day launch ad budget (already in tooling_and_nre) hot to seed review velocity, enroll an initial batch in Vine, and lead with the honest-limitation bullets so early reviewers arrive with calibrated expectations instead of mismatched ones that turn into 1-stars.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Vine enrollment plus landed cost of ~20-30 seeded units.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and a production lot shipped with 0.8mm buckle steel instead of the specified 1.2mm gauge — it passed the factory's quick pull test but started cracking at the anchor after a few customers' repeated ratcheting cycles, reproducing the exact C1 failure the whole hero idea existed to prevent, and a wave of 'buckle cracked again' one-star reviews hit right as the rating was building.
premortem.mitigation: Per-lot gauge-caliper check on incoming buckle steel (the brief's own stated mitigation) plus the 1,000-cycle destructive fatigue pull-test on a sample from every production lot, not just the pilot lot, before that lot is released to FBA.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Recurring per-lot caliper check plus destructive sample testing, applied to every production run after the pilot.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and after several production runs the stamping die's radiused deburr edge wore back toward a sharp sheared edge without anyone noticing on the line, so later lots quietly reintroduced the micro-abrasion failure point F6 identifies, and the rating dipped right as volume was ramping.
premortem.mitigation: Add a radius-edge visual/gauge check to the existing per-lot QC step (same inspector, adds minutes not a new hire) and schedule die maintenance/re-sharpening on a fixed stamping-count interval rather than a calendar interval.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Incremental QC inspection time plus periodic die maintenance across the production run.

regulatory: No mandatory US safety certification expected for a passive steel/nylon travel accessory; confirm Prop 65 labelling treatment given the numeric '150KG' strength claim on packaging.
No CPSC magnet scrutiny: product contains no magnets and is not marketed to or clearly used by children.
Standard customs/HTS duty classification only (6307.90.9891 per scout, plus Chapter 99 Section 301 subheading 9903.88.15), already reflected in the duty-rate economics inputs.

Amazon claims-substantiation risk on the '150KG PER BUCKLE, pull-tested' claim: back it with the third-party fatigue/pull-test report (budgeted in tooling_and_nre) and phrase it as a tested figure, not a safety or weight-capacity guarantee, per the pre-mortem's claim-suppression obituary.
three_sentences_to_founder: The hero buckle is the right call at a landed cost near $2.83 per 2-pack set (about 14% of a $19.99 price, comfortably inside the 30%-of-price rail), but the die modification plus the mandatory FTO clearance push first sale to roughly 32-54 weeks (43 weeks base) — it genuinely waits on tooling lead time, not on the design being wrong, so the 0-month timeline in the brief is not achievable for this version.

Ship the lean v1 (hero buckle I1 + bar-tack reinforcement I2 + raw steel finish I6, ~$9,650-$41,100 in launch tooling/NRE) rather than the full four-idea plan: base-case contribution lands around 21% of price, which clears the 15% no-go floor but misses the 25% healthy line mainly on launch-phase ad spend, so adding a second overmold-tooling line (I3) and its own FTO exposure before any sales data exists is not worth doing yet — add I3, I4 and I5 as fast-follows once ~30 reviews validate demand, exactly as innovaty's own v2_later logic already suggests.

Year-one volume is a wide $3,500-$22,800-unit range (base ~10,300) because scout could not fetch real tracker data for this term, and two of the seven pre-mortem risks — review velocity stalling below the moore.chasm threshold, and a supplier substituting thinner 0.8mm buckle steel — are rated fatal-impact; they only stay survivable because their mitigations (Vine-seeded reviews, per-lot gauge and destructive pull-testing) are funded in this plan now, not promised for later.
